title: Apps
intro: Everything you can install into Tel-Agent, running on your own machine. Channel apps are the ones that carry conversations — phone, WhatsApp, Telegram — and every one of them goes through the same agent, the same routing rules, and the same searchable history.
installed_failed: The installed applications could not be read.
refused_note: These did not load. The reason is the server's own words.
empty_body: The core applications register themselves when the server starts, so an empty list here means the server is running without its catalogue. The store below is the roadmap.
store_note: Apps are pulled from the registry and run on your own machine. Nothing is sent anywhere unless the app itself talks to an outside service, which is stated on the card.
mcp_title: Anything with an API is already an integration
mcp_body_after: have no app of their own and do not need one — point Tel-Agent at an MCP server on your network and its tools become things the agent can do on a call. You are not waiting on us to write a connector.
write_body: An app is a small container that speaks one of the Tel-Agent protocols: a channel receives a message and hands it to the agent, a tool exposes a function the agent may call. Anything with an API can become one.
offline_title: Two channels are down — phone line and WhatsApp
offline_body_after: and the WhatsApp session was logged out from the phone. Messages sent to either are not reaching the agent.
error_title: A channel app crashed on startup
error_body: The Telegram channel app quit twice while starting and Tel-Agent stopped loading the rest of the list. Your phone line is unaffected and still answering. Disable that app to get the other channels back.
cat_channels_note: Ways a conversation can reach the agent.
cat_calendars_note: Reading free slots and writing bookings.
cat_tools_note: Things the agent may do during a call.
cat_notifications_note: How you find out something needs a human.
cat_pbx_note: For teams that already own a phone system and are not replacing it.
cat_sip_note: Carrier presets. The generic trunk already covers any of them.
cat_health_note: Clinic and pharmacy software, mostly local and mostly without a public API.
cat_analytics_note: Watching how the agent actually behaves.
app_agent_core_desc: The model runner every assistant speaks through. Required — replacing it swaps the whole reasoning engine.
app_german_voices_desc: Speech synthesis for the phone channel. Four voices, all generated on this machine.
app_database_desc: Stores calls, transcripts and contacts. Nothing works without it.
app_tls_certificates_desc: Renews the certificate for your web chat and admin interface automatically.
app_signal_desc: End-to-end encrypted messaging. Runs entirely on your machine — no business account needed.
app_sms_desc: Plain text messages through your existing SMS gateway. Good for confirmations and reminders.
app_web_chat_desc: A chat bubble on your own site. The agent answers with the same knowledge sources.
app_email_desc: Reads a shared mailbox and replies as the agent. Threads appear next to calls.
app_instagram_dm_desc: Direct messages from your company page. Meta rate limits apply.
app_matrix_desc: Self-hosted messaging for teams that already run their own homeserver.
app_caldav_desc: Two-way sync with Nextcloud, Radicale or any CalDAV server. Lets the agent read free slots and book.
app_google_calendar_desc: Same booking behaviour against a Google account. Sends your free/busy data to Google.
app_local_transcription_desc: Whisper running on this machine. Slower than the cloud on old hardware, but nothing leaves the building.
app_spam_list_desc: A shared list of nuisance numbers, refreshed daily. Feeds the blocking rules.
app_backup_desc: Nightly encrypted copies of recordings and transcripts to a disk or S3 bucket you own.
app_slack_desc: Posts failed tool calls and missed calls into a channel your team already watches.
app_ntfy_desc: Push alerts to your phone from your own ntfy server. No account anywhere.
app_asterisk_freepbx_desc: Sits beside a PBX you already run. Tel-Agent becomes an extension, so desk phones keep working exactly as they do now.
app_3cx_desc: Registers as a SIP extension on 3CX, cloud or self-hosted. Call routing stays in 3CX; the agent answers what you send it.
app_yeastar_desc: Hardware and cloud PBX. Tested on the P-series; older S-series needs the legacy SIP profile.
app_pascom_desc: Cloud PBX with a documented REST API. Extension registration works; presence sync does not yet.
app_nfon_desc: The largest cloud PBX in the DACH region. Needs their partner API, which we have applied for.
app_starface_desc: Cloud and hybrid PBX common in German practices. Their module SDK is the intended route.
app_swyx_enreach_desc: UCaaS across DACH and Benelux. No public API for extension registration yet.
app_innovaphone_desc: Hybrid PBX for the German mid-market. Their SDK requires a partner agreement.
app_wildix_desc: UCaaS with its own call-routing layer. Integration would duplicate our routing rules — low priority.
app_teams_phone_desc: Direct Routing through a certified SBC. Works today if you configure the SBC by hand as a plain SIP trunk.
app_generic_sip_trunk_desc: Host, username, password. Any carrier that speaks SIP works here, including every carrier listed in this category.
app_easybell_presets_desc: Presets for easybell trunks: codecs, registration interval and the outbound caller-ID rules they expect.
app_sipgate_desc: Presets plus their number-provisioning API, so new numbers appear here without a support ticket.
app_telekom_companyflex_desc: Works as a plain trunk. The preset handles their unusual registration timing.
app_telekom_companyflex_warn: Registration drops on IP change — set a static IP.
app_toplink_desc: Premium DACH partner for SIP trunking. Plain trunk config works meanwhile.
app_ecotel_desc: Whitelabel carrier. Plain trunk config works meanwhile.
app_twilio_desc: Elastic SIP trunking and numbers in most countries, bought by the minute with no contract. The quickest way to a second number for testing — and the most expensive way to run a practice line all year.
app_a1_telekom_austria_desc: Austrian landlines and porting. Presets contributed by two Vienna businesses.
app_tomedo_desc: Patient records and appointments. Reachable today through an MCP server that speaks Tomedo's local API — read-only is the safe default.
app_ivoris_desc: Dental practice software. An MCP wrapper around its SQL database is the working route; ask your Ivoris partner first.
app_dr_flex_desc: Reads free slots and books appointments. Confirmations go out through their system, not ours.
app_dr_flex_warn: Early build — verify every booking for the first week.
app_samedi_desc: Booking platform used across German specialist practices. Their API needs a practice contract.
app_doctolib_desc: Their partner API is closed to self-hosted software today. We ask again each quarter.
app_latido_desc: Austrian practice software. No public API; an MCP wrapper is the likely route.
app_pharmacy_stock_win_pharma_lgpi_desc: Prescription and stock lookups over the counter phone. Both run locally, so an MCP server on the same network reaches them.
app_onoffice_desc: Looks up listings and books viewings during a call. Uses their documented REST API.
app_casavi_desc: Tenant requests and building management. Creates a ticket from a call with the transcript attached.
app_immoware24_desc: Tenant data and property enquiries. API access needs their partner programme.
app_domus_desc: Widely used in German property management. No public API.
app_etg24_desc: Resident notifications and requests. Their API is open enough that an MCP wrapper works well.
app_propstack_desc: Property details and CRM records. Straightforward REST API behind an MCP server.
app_mews_desc: Room availability, reservations and guest requests. Their API is the best documented in this category.
app_opentable_desc: Table availability and bookings. Rate limits are strict — cache availability for a minute.
app_resmio_desc: Restaurant table bookings. Works; cancellations still have to be done in resmio.
app_protel_desc: Front-desk tasks and room bookings. Their API is version-dependent.
app_smoobu_desc: Holiday-let reservations and availability across channels. Clean REST API.
app_toast_desc: Restaurant POS and orders. US-first; low priority for DACH.
app_datev_desc: Effectively mandatory for German tax advisors. Their API requires certification, which takes months.
app_bexio_desc: Invoices, contacts and orders for Swiss businesses. Good REST API behind an MCP server.
app_odoo_desc: ERP modules for sales, stock and customers. Self-hosted Odoo is the easy case.
app_stripe_desc: Payment status and invoice lookups. Never let the agent take card numbers over the phone.
app_stripe_warn: Card capture by voice is off by design.
app_selectline_desc: ERP for orders, stock and customer data.
app_planity_desc: Salon appointments and stylist schedules. Popular in France and Germany.
app_phorest_desc: Salon bookings, client records and reminders.
app_booksy_desc: Beauty and wellness bookings. Public API works behind an MCP server.
app_langfuse_desc: Traces every agent turn: which tool was called, what it returned, how long it took. Self-hostable, so traces stay with you.
app_fireflies_ai_desc: Sends transcripts out for searchable notes. Read the privacy note before switching this on for customer calls.
app_gong_desc: Sales call intelligence. Aimed at large sales teams.
app_grafana_desc: Exports call counts, latency and tool failures as Prometheus metrics for a dashboard you already have.
